message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
jobs:
  test-non-windows:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        rust: [stable]
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macOS-latest]
    steps:
      - name: Install Nix
        uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@v3
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v1
      - name: Check Nix flake inputs
        uses: DeterminateSystems/flake-checker-action@v2
        with:
          fail-mode: true
      - name: Build and run tests
        run: nix flake check

  test-windows:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        rust: [stable]
        os: [windows-latest]
    steps:
      - name: Setup Rust
        uses: hecrj/setup-rust-action@master
        with:
          rust-version: ${{ matrix.rust }}
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - name: Installing LibClang on Windows
        shell: pwsh
        run: choco install -y llvm
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v1
      - name: Cache cargo dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache
            ~/.cargo/registry/index
            ~/.cargo/git
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-
      - name: Build the crate
        run: cargo build --release
      # - name: Run Tests
      #   run: cargo test
",
  "rationale": "The Windows job downloads Cargo dependencies on every run. The repository has a Cargo.lock file, satisfying the pattern's precondition that cache inputs include a lockfile. The experiment evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200) demonstrates 20% elapsed time savings by caching Gradle dependencies with actions/cache@v4; the same mechanism applies to Cargo's ~/.cargo/registry and ~/.cargo/git directories. The non-Windows job uses Nix which manages its own store; caching it would require Nix-specific infrastructure not covered by the general GHA cache pattern. No other pattern has both measured evidence and clear applicability to this workflow.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200"]
}

- The workflow uses `actions/checkout@v1` which is very old (current is v4)
- The non-Windows job uses Nix with `nix flake check` which builds and runs tests
- The Windows job uses cargo directly
- There's a Cargo.lock file, so dependencies are pinned
- The workflow runs on push and pull_request
